items.statement: Evidence for Relative Gibbs stability of the intact trans/cis ketoester pair
items.expected: Actual comparable endpoint free energies place50/trans belowS20/cis for the intact neutral-singlet local epimer pair, preserving every other stereocenter. State the medium, temperature and conformational scope actually represented and relate them to the supplied23°C experiment with its unresolvedTHF/MeOH composition. A supported same-condition full-molecule comparison is eligible without a hidden pureMeOH/298.15K source route. Compositionally different acid/enol species or a protonation barrier cannot establish this product ordering. Assess the disclosed intact-pair methanol/298.15 K baseline or an evidence-backed comparable substitution, keeping it distinct from the 23 degrees C mixed-solvent experiment. Source free-energy differences are evidence context, not targets.

items.statement: Evidence for Equilibrium implication and its relation to the reversible experiment
items.expected: From the actual computed cis-minus-trans Gibbs difference and explicit common-temperature Boltzmann/detailed-balance relation, show the trans-biased equilibrium implication, consistent with recovery of trans under reversible epimerization and substantially more trans-biased than the 1.1:1 single-pass outcome. State which solvent and conformational model this establishes. Do not equate this model equilibrium with the 30 min mixed-solvent experiment or award credit for merely repeating the observed trans outcome.

items.statement: Evidence for Fixed endpoint thermodynamics does not determine finite-time protonolysis selectivity
items.expected: Demonstrate with an explicit physically coherent reaction-network/kinetic analysis or equivalent quantitative construction that the same endpoint free-energy difference can admit different finite-timeT/C outcomes when formation barriers/rates or preparation history differ. Any reversible branch must satisfy the same detailed-balance ratio. This is a non-identifiability result; merely missing aTS, asserting uncertainty or proposing unexecuted calculations fails.

items.statement: Evidence for Local stereochemical origin of access to both ketoester epimers
items.expected: Explain with atom-mapped local geometry and evidence-backed stereochemical/kinetic reasoning that C6 becomes planar in the tetrasubstituted O-TMS enol ether and its protonolysis restores the local stereocenter, allowing access to both epimers while preserving the rest of the polycycle. Distinguish this structural explanation from proof of a unique acid-face transition state or exact branching ratio. The cumulative 70% recycled cis yield is not intrinsic stability or single-pass selectivity. A demonstrated equivalent stereochemical account passes directly.
